headline: Large User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, such as data centers, to pay for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity, preventing these costs from being passed on to residential customers.
supporters: Residential ratepayers, Senator L. Louise Lucas
news_headline: Virginia Shifts Data Center Energy Costs to Users
news_summary: Virginia HB 1393 directs the primary electric provider to petition the SCC to establish rates for recovering increased electric generating capacity costs. The bill mandates that customers with 25 MW or more in electric demand, including data centers, bear these costs, preventing them from being passed to other customers.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities providing water to data centers to report the total volume of water consumed by these facilities to the State Water Control Board, increasing transparency.
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, environmental advocates, communities
news_headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency Bill Passes
news_summary: SB 553 mandates water utilities to report the volume of water consumed by data centers to the State Water Control Board, aiming to provide communities with clearer insight into local resource use. This measure addresses growing concerns about the significant water needs of the data center industry.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities like data centers, requiring site assessments for sound profiles near homes and schools, and allowing localities to assess environmental impacts.
supporters: Del. Joshua Thomas, Del. John McAuliff, community advocates/residents
news_headline: New Data Center Siting Requirements Passed in Virginia
news_summary: HB 153 creates a permit process for high-energy-use facilities, requiring site assessments to examine sound profiles near residential areas and schools. It also grants localities the option to assess potential impacts on ground and surface water, agriculture, and historic resources.
